story_type: moon rover driven flat out in a speed test, 1972 mission film
hook: Driving a car flat out, on the Moon.
narration: This is a car being driven flat out, on the Moon.
Apollo 16, April 1972. Charlie Duke filmed while John Young put the rover through a full test.
Young threw it into sharp turns. At one point it had about two wheels on the ground.
In one sixth gravity, every bump sends the rover airborne, and with no air, dust flies in long clean arcs.
[short pause] Duke called out a big rooster tail at all four wheels.
outcome: The rover came through its Grand Prix, and Young and Duke drove it back to base to close out their first moonwalk.
title: Moon rover driven flat out
description:
On April 21, 1972, Apollo 16 commander John Young drove the lunar rover through a speed and handling test while Charlie Duke filmed, near their landing site in the Descartes highlands. From the 1972 NASA film Apollo 16: Nothing So Hidden.

Footage: NASA video (Apollo 16: Nothing So Hidden, 1972), via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_16_-_Nothing_So_Hidden.webm
